name: faith
quote: My hearts says she's going to be ok.
description: Confidence in the accuracy of a belief about something or someone not based on rational proof or experience.
perceptions: An outcome I prefer is going to happen.
There are other things that could happen, but I'm sure my preferred outcome will be the one.

guidance.description: There are many resources for cultivating faith. A key theme is trusting that it’s going to be okay in the long run regardless of what’s currently happening.

variations.name: existential faith
variations.description: Believing without evidence in the accuracy of a framework of statements and predictions about reality.
perceptions: I trust that certain things to be true about existence.
There are other things that could happen, but if so, I'm sure there's a reason for it.
examples: Cheaters always get what they deserve.
My religion will guide me to a better afterlife.

comparisons.description: If someone is certain from their faith, the source of that certainty is not justifiable from experience or logic -- it's a form of trust. On the other hand, when if you're _mentally_ certain about something, the source is not based on an external trust, but it's from past experience or logic.

commentaries.quote: Faith is believing that the outcome will be what it should be, no matter what it is.
Faith is not something to grasp, it is a state to grow into.
Faith is taking the first step even when you don't see the whole staircase.
Faith is not belief without proof, but trust without reservation.
